caption: The drawing depicts a group of people gathered around a central figure who is lying on a large wooden cross. The central figure, depicted with a beard and wearing only a cloth around the waist, has red marks on the body, suggesting wounds. Several individuals are actively participating in the scene: one person is using a hammer to drive a nail into the central figure’s right hand, another is pulling on a rope tied to the left arm, and others are adjusting the position of the cross or holding the limbs. At least two figures, wearing grayish armor and helmets with plumes, are positioned at the left and right sides and appear to be Roman soldiers. Behind the main action, a group of onlookers, most dressed in reddish or brownish robes, stand close together, with some holding their hands in front of them. The background consists of earthy tones such as brown, green, and blue, and the drawing incorporates muted shades of red, beige, and gray throughout the clothing and the environment. The artwork is bordered by a plain, off-white margin and is signed in the bottom right corner.
title: Stations of the Cross No. 11. "Jesus is Nailed to the Cross
